text:
Mira: FYI — customer AcmeOps just reported embeddings switched width after we promoted a canary. They pinned to their variant but downstream index exploded. Request ID: req_0a9b3c. Observed: embedding length = 1536 (expected 1024). Payload:

Mira: sample request (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/semantic-embed-1024","input":"The quick brown fox"}'
```

Mira: response excerpt (trimmed):
```
{"embedding": [0.0123, -0.0045, ..., 0.0021]}  // length reported by client: 1536
```

Mira: customer says this started immediately after our canary roll; they had pinned alias `acme/sem-embed` to what they thought was 1024. They couldn't ingest vectors into their index because vector dimension mismatch. Blocking their pipeline.

Devon: can you confirm the alias mapping and the exact model string they used? any chance they accidentally requested a different model id?

Mira: They gave us the header they set: `X-Model-Alias: acme/sem-embed` and the API call above. From support logs their SDK resolved alias to `redwood/semantic-embed-1024@stable-lock` at 03:42 UTC but our routing.log shows a fallback to `redwood/semantic-embed-1536:v3` for capacity reasons.

Jordan: grabbing routing log snippet: 
```
2024-11-02T03:42:10Z request=req_0a9b3c select_model alias=acme/sem-embed -> candidate=[semantic-embed-1024@stable-lock, semantic-embed-1536:v3] reason=capacity selected=semantic-embed-1536:v3
```

Jordan: so looks like alias resolved to multiple compatible variants and our smart routing chose the 1536 variant as fallback. That would produce a longer vector even if the alias name implies 1024.

Samira: That checks out — we had a canary that introduced a 1536-width variant (improved semantic coverage for long docs). Alias resolution policy should have respected pinned variants for customers with locks. Need to check whether our alias metadata included the pinned flag.

Mira: Customer insisted they used a pinned variant; their UI shows `acme/sem-embed -> semantic-embed-1024@stable-lock`. Could be our alias sync to the runtime was delayed.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed: canary id cny-2024-11-02-0340 by ops-team (variants: semantic-embed-1536:v3 added to routing table)

Devon: immediate mitigation options:
- Force override for that customer: set runtime policy to prefer `semantic-embed-1024@stable-lock` for alias `acme/sem-embed`
- Customer-side: set `model=redwood/semantic-embed-1024@stable-lock` explicitly in API call (temporary)
- Revert canary alias exposure if alias leak is confirmed

Jordan: commands to inspect/rollback alias mapping: 
```
# inspect
redwoodctl alias get acme/sem-embed --env=prod
# force map
redwoodctl alias set acme/sem-embed redwood/semantic-embed-1024@stable-lock --force --reason="hotfix: acme dim mismatch"
```

Samira: also please grab a small sample of the first 8 floats from both a 1536 and 1024 response so we can fingerprint which variant generated it. the embedding float ranges differ slightly (we can compute checksum).

Mira: provided sample from customer (first 8 floats):
`[0.0123, -0.0045, 0.0011, 0.0099, -0.0022, 0.0033, -0.0017, 0.0006]`

Jordan: that sequence matches our semantic-embed-1536:v3 samples (we keep a sample db). I pushed an emergency alias set to force the stable-lock mapping and invalidated the routing cache for their tenant.

Mira: after the alias fix I asked the customer to retry — they reported immediate recovery: embeddings returned length 1024 and their index ingestion resumed. Confirmed by their error logs showing no more "vec length mismatch".

Samira: root cause action item: investigate why the alias resolution allowed fallback to a different-width variant when a customer-level pinned lock existed. Possible causes: timing window during canary rollout where pinned flag wasn't yet propagated, or an upgrade to the variant metadata schema that dropped the `width` attribute.

Samira: next steps:
- Eng-ML to add a validation check on alias creation that all candidate variants have same vector dimension when alias is advertised as "fixed-width"
- Runtime to ensure pinned locks are enforced at routing decision time (no fallback to different-width variants)
- Add a post-rollout invariant test that sends a small probe for a set of customers with pinned variants to verify dimension stability

Mira: customer is unblocked and asked for a postmortem + commit we used to rollback. Provided them with the command we ran and ticket ID SUP-2024-4839. They asked for a note in the change log for future transparency.

Devon: I'll file infra bug and track the timing propagation metric. Jordan, Samira — can you own the runtime and ml checks respectively?

Jordan: taking runtime check. I'll add an alert if alias mapping changes to expose candidate variants with mismatched vector widths.

Samira: taking the validation rule and post-rollout probe.

Mira: thanks team. Closing the customer escalation after we deliver a short incident note. :thumbsup:
